sanskrit: na hi te mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ bhūṣaṇair api varjitam asahāyā narebhyaś ca nodvijasy amaraprabhe
english: For your form is not merely human — even without ornaments you are not alarmed, unaccompanied, before men, O one who has the splendour of an immortal.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasyā bhaimī vacanam abravīt mānuṣīṃ māṃ vijānīhi bhartāraṃ samanuvratām
english: Hearing those words, the daughter of Bhīma spoke in reply: Know me as a human woman, wholly devoted to following my husband.

sanskrit: sairandhrīṃ jātisaṃpannāṃ bhujiṣyāṃ kāmavāsinīm phalamūlāśanām ekāṃ yatrasāyaṃpratiśrayām
english: I am a skilled sairandhrī attendant, a free woman living by choice, subsisting on fruits and roots alone, sheltering wherever evening finds me.

sanskrit: asaṃkhyeyaguṇo bhartā māṃ ca nityam anuvrataḥ bhartāram api taṃ vīraṃ chāyevānapagā sadā
english: My husband is of virtues beyond counting, and he was ever faithful to me; I too followed that hero like his own shadow, never departing.

sanskrit: tasya daivāt prasaṅgo 'bhūd atimātraṃ sma devane dyūte sa nirjitaś caiva vanam eko 'bhyupeyivān
english: By fate an excessive addiction to gaming came upon him; defeated at dice, he went alone into the forest.

sanskrit: tam ekavasanaṃ vīram unmattam iva vihvalam āśvāsayantī bhartāram aham anvagamaṃ vanam
english: Comforting that hero, clad in a single garment, distraught and seeming maddened, I followed my husband into the forest.

sanskrit: sa kadā cid vane vīraḥ kasmiṃś cit kāraṇāntare kṣutparītaḥ suvimanās tad apy ekaṃ vyasarjayat
english: Then that hero, overcome with hunger in the forest for some other reason, deeply troubled in mind, even cast away that one garment.

sanskrit: tam ekavasanaṃ nagnam unmattaṃ gatacetasam anuvrajantī bahulā na svapāmi niśāḥ sadā
english: Following him — naked, having shed his single garment, maddened, bereft of his senses — I spent many nights without sleep.

sanskrit: tato bahutithe kāle suptām utsṛjya māṃ kva cit vāsaso 'rdhaṃ paricchidya tyaktavān mām anāgasam
english: Then, after a long while, he abandoned me as I lay sleeping — cutting off half the garment, he forsook me, blameless though I was.

sanskrit: taṃ mārgamāṇā bhartāraṃ dahyamānā dinakṣapāḥ na vindāmy amaraprakhyaṃ priyaṃ prāṇadhaneśvaram
english: Searching for that husband, burning with grief through days and nights, I cannot find my beloved — he who is like an immortal, the lord of my life and wealth.

sanskrit: tām aśruparipūrṇākṣīṃ vilapantīṃ tathā bahu rājamātābravīd ārtāṃ bhaimīm ārtatarā svayam
english: Seeing her weeping, her eyes filled with tears, lamenting greatly — the queen mother, herself deeply distressed, spoke to the anguished daughter of Bhīma.

sanskrit: vasasva mayi kalyāṇi prītir me tvayi vartate mṛgayiṣyanti te bhadre bhartāraṃ puruṣā mama
english: Dwell with me, O auspicious one — my heart goes out to you; O fortunate lady, my men will search for your husband.

sanskrit: atha vā svayam āgacchet paridhāvann itas tataḥ ihaiva vasatī bhadre bhartāram upalapsyase
english: Or perhaps he himself will come, wandering here and there; staying here, dear one, you will meet your husband.

sanskrit: rājamātur vacaḥ śrutvā damayantī vaco 'bravīt samayenotsahe vastuṃ tvayi vīraprajāyini
english: Hearing the queen mother's words, Damayantī replied: I am willing to stay with you, O mother of heroes, but only on certain conditions.

sanskrit: ucchiṣṭaṃ naiva bhuñjīyāṃ na kuryāṃ pādadhāvanam na cāhaṃ puruṣān anyān saṃbhāṣeyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: I will never eat leavings, nor wash the feet of others, nor will I converse with any man under any circumstance.

sanskrit: prārthayed yadi māṃ kaś cid daṇḍyas te sa pumān bhavet bhartur anveṣaṇārthaṃ tu paśyeyaṃ brāhmaṇān aham
english: Should any man importune me, let him be punished by you; but to seek my husband I should be permitted to meet with brahmin men.

sanskrit: yady evam iha kartavyaṃ vasāmy aham asaṃśayam ato 'nyathā na me vāso vartate hṛdaye kva cit
english: If these conditions can be observed here, I will stay without doubt; otherwise, to remain anywhere holds no place in my heart.

sanskrit: tāṃ prahṛṣṭena manasā rājamātedam abravīt sarvam etat kariṣyāmi diṣṭyā te vratam īdṛśam
english: With a gladdened heart the queen mother spoke to her: All this I will grant — how fortunate is your vow of such a kind!

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato bhaimīṃ rājamātā viśāṃ pate uvācedaṃ duhitaraṃ sunandāṃ nāma bhārata
english: Having spoken thus to the daughter of Bhīma, O lord of the people, the queen mother then addressed her daughter named Sunandā, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sairandhrīm abhijānīṣva sunande devarūpiṇīm etayā saha modasva nirudvignamanāḥ svayam
english: Know this sairandhrī, O Sunandā, as one whose form is divine; rejoice freely with her, your heart at ease.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca utsṛjya damayantīṃ tu nalo rājā viśāṃ pate dadarśa dāvaṃ dahyantaṃ mahāntaṃ gahane vane
english: Bṛhadaśva said: After abandoning Damayantī, O lord of the people, king Nala beheld a great forest fire blazing in the deep woods.

sanskrit: tatra śuśrāva madhye 'gnau śabdaṃ bhūtasya kasya cit abhidhāva nalety uccaiḥ puṇyaśloketi cāsakṛt
english: There in the midst of the fire he heard the voice of some creature crying out loudly, again and again: "Run here, Nala! O Puṇyaśloka!"

sanskrit: mā bhair iti nalaś coktvā madhyam agneḥ praviśya tam dadarśa nāgarājānaṃ śayānaṃ kuṇḍalīkṛtam
english: Saying "Fear not!" Nala entered into the midst of the fire and saw the king of serpents lying there, coiled in a ring.

sanskrit: sa nāgaḥ prāñjalir bhūtvā vepamāno nalaṃ tadā uvāca viddhi māṃ rājan nāgaṃ karkoṭakaṃ nṛpa
english: That serpent, joining his palms in supplication and trembling, then spoke to Nala: Know me, O king, as the serpent Karkoṭaka, O lord.

sanskrit: mayā pralabdho brahmarṣir anāgāḥ sumahātapāḥ tena manyuparītena śapto 'smi manujādhipa
english: I deceived a sinless brahmin seer of great ascetic power; enraged by that, he cursed me, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tasya śāpān na śaknomi padād vicalituṃ padam upadekṣyāmi te śreyas trātum arhati māṃ bhavān
english: Because of his curse I cannot move a single step from this spot; I will point out the path of good to you — you should rescue me.

sanskrit: sakhā ca te bhaviṣyāmi matsamo nāsti pannagaḥ laghuś ca te bhaviṣyāmi śīghram ādāya gaccha mām
english: I will become your ally — there is no serpent equal to me; I will make myself light — quickly take me up and go.

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa nāgendro babhūvāṅguṣṭhamātrakaḥ taṃ gṛhītvā nalaḥ prāyād uddeśaṃ dāvavarjitam
english: Having said this, the lord of serpents shrank to the size of a thumb; taking him up, Nala proceeded toward a region free of the forest fire.

sanskrit: ākāśadeśam āsādya vimuktaṃ kṛṣṇavartmanā utsraṣṭukāmaṃ taṃ nāgaḥ punaḥ karkoṭako 'bravīt
english: Having reached an open place, free from the dark-pathed fire, as Nala was about to release him, the serpent Karkoṭaka spoke again.

sanskrit: padāni gaṇayan gaccha svāni naiṣadha kāni cit tatra te 'haṃ mahārāja śreyo dhāsyāmi yat param
english: Go counting your own steps, O Naiṣadha — a certain number; there, O great king, I will bestow on you the highest good.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃkhyātum ārabdham adaśad daśame pade tasya daṣṭasya tad rūpaṃ kṣipram antaradhīyata
english: Then, as Nala began to count, the serpent bit him at the tenth step; the form of the bitten man quickly vanished.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā vismitas tasthāv ātmānaṃ vikṛtaṃ nalaḥ svarūpadhāriṇaṃ nāgaṃ dadarśa ca mahīpatiḥ
english: Nala stood astonished to behold himself transformed; the lord of the earth saw that the serpent now bore his own natural form.

sanskrit: tataḥ karkoṭako nāgaḥ sāntvayan nalam abravīt mayā te 'ntarhitaṃ rūpaṃ na tvā vidyur janā iti
english: Then the serpent Karkoṭaka, consoling Nala, said: I have concealed your appearance so that people may not recognise you.

sanskrit: yatkṛte cāsi vikṛto duḥkhena mahatā nala viṣeṇa sa madīyena tvayi duḥkhaṃ nivatsyati
english: He for whose sake you have been transformed and suffered great grief — that one, through my venom now lodged within you, will dwell in torment.

sanskrit: viṣeṇa saṃvṛtair gātrair yāvat tvāṃ na vimokṣyati tāvat tvayi mahārāja duḥkhaṃ vai sa nivatsyati
english: So long as he does not release you, the venom pervading your limbs will persist in him, O great king — he shall abide in suffering.

sanskrit: anāgā yena nikṛtas tvam anarho janādhipa krodhād asūyayitvā taṃ rakṣā me bhavataḥ kṛtā
english: By him who wronged you without cause, O lord of men — undeservedly, out of jealousy and anger — you were deceived; this protection I have now rendered you.

sanskrit: na te bhayaṃ naravyāghra daṃṣṭribhyaḥ śatruto 'pi vā brahmavidbhyaś ca bhavitā matprasādān narādhipa
english: You shall have no fear, O tiger among men, from fanged creatures, from enemies, or from those learned in sacred lore — by my grace, O lord of men.

sanskrit: rājan viṣanimittā ca na te pīḍā bhaviṣyati saṃgrāmeṣu ca rājendra śaśvaj jayam avāpsyasi
english: By reason of my venom, O king, no affliction shall come to you; and in battles, O lord of kings, you shall always win victory.

sanskrit: gaccha rājann itaḥ sūto bāhuko 'ham iti bruvan samīpam ṛtuparṇasya sa hi vedākṣanaipuṇam ayodhyāṃ nagarīṃ ramyām adyaiva niṣadheśvara
english: Go from here, O king, presenting yourself as a charioteer saying "I am Bāhuka," to the court of Ṛtuparṇa — for he knows the science of dice — into the lovely city of Ayodhyā, this very day, O lord of Niṣadha.

sanskrit: sa te 'kṣahṛdayaṃ dātā rājāśvahṛdayena vai ikṣvākukulajaḥ śrīmān mitraṃ caiva bhaviṣyati
english: That glorious king, born in the Ikṣvāku line, will give you the secret of dice in exchange for the secret of horses, and will become your friend.

sanskrit: bhaviṣyasi yadākṣajñaḥ śreyasā yokṣyase tadā sameṣyasi ca dārais tvaṃ mā sma śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ rājyena tanayābhyāṃ ca satyam etad bravīmi te
english: When you have mastered the lore of dice you will be joined with good fortune; then you will be reunited with your wife — do not give your mind to grief — and with your kingdom and your children. I speak the truth to you.

sanskrit: svarūpaṃ ca yadā draṣṭum icchethās tvaṃ narādhipa saṃsmartavyas tadā te 'haṃ vāsaś cedaṃ nivāsayeḥ
english: And when you wish to behold your true form, O lord of men, you must remember me then and put on this garment.

sanskrit: anena vāsasācchannaḥ svarūpaṃ pratipatsyase ity uktvā pradadāv asmai divyaṃ vāsoyugaṃ tadā
english: Clothed in this garment you will recover your own form — so saying, he then bestowed upon him a divine pair of garments.

sanskrit: evaṃ nalaṃ samādiśya vāso dattvā ca kaurava nāgarājas tato rājaṃs tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Having thus instructed Nala and given him the garments, O Kaurava, the king of serpents then vanished from that very spot, O king.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca tasminn antarhite nāge prayayau naiṣadho nalaḥ ṛtuparṇasya nagaraṃ prāviśad daśame 'hani
english: Bṛhadaśva said: When the serpent had vanished, Naiṣadha Nala set forth and entered the city of Ṛtuparṇa on the tenth day.

sanskrit: sa rājānam upātiṣṭhad bāhuko 'ham iti bruvan aśvānāṃ vāhane yuktaḥ pṛthivyāṃ nāsti matsamaḥ
english: He presented himself to the king, saying "I am Bāhuka"; in the driving of horses on this earth there is none my equal.

sanskrit: arthakṛcchreṣu caivāhaṃ praṣṭavyo naipuṇeṣu ca annasaṃskāram api ca jānāmy anyair viśeṣataḥ
english: In matters of difficulty and in the arts, I am also worth consulting; in the preparation of food I have skill that surpasses others.

sanskrit: yāni śilpāni loke 'smin yac cāpy anyat suduṣkaram sarvaṃ yatiṣye tat kartum ṛtuparṇa bharasva mām
english: Whatever crafts exist in this world and whatever else is hard to accomplish, I will strive to do it all — employ me, Ṛtuparṇa.

sanskrit: ṛtuparṇa uvāca vasa bāhuka bhadraṃ te sarvam etat kariṣyasi śīghrayāne sadā buddhir dhīyate me viśeṣataḥ
english: Ṛtuparṇa said: Stay, Bāhuka, good fortune to you; you shall do all of this — in the matter of swift driving my thoughts are especially fixed.

sanskrit: sa tvam ātiṣṭha yogaṃ taṃ yena śīghrā hayā mama bhaveyur aśvādhyakṣo 'si vetanaṃ te śataṃ śatāḥ
english: You therefore apply your skill so that my horses may be swift; you are superintendent of horses — your wages are a hundred of hundreds.

sanskrit: tvām upasthāsyataś cemau nityaṃ vārṣṇeyajīvalau etābhyāṃ raṃsyase sārdhaṃ vasa vai mayi bāhuka
english: These two, Vārṣṇeya and Jīvala, shall constantly attend upon you; you shall find enjoyment in their company — stay with me, Bāhuka.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca evam ukto nalas tena nyavasat tatra pūjitaḥ ṛtuparṇasya nagare sahavārṣṇeyajīvalaḥ
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Thus addressed by him, Nala dwelt there, honoured, in the city of Ṛtuparṇa, together with Vārṣṇeya and Jīvala.

sanskrit: sa tatra nivasan rājā vaidarbhīm anucintayan sāyaṃ sāyaṃ sadā cemaṃ ślokam ekaṃ jagāda ha
english: Dwelling there, the king, brooding constantly on the daughter of Vidarbha, would sing this one verse aloud each and every evening.

sanskrit: kva nu sā kṣutpipāsārtā śrāntā śete tapasvinī smarantī tasya mandasya kaṃ vā sādyopatiṣṭhati
english: Where now does she lie — weary, afflicted by hunger and thirst, that suffering woman — remembering that foolish one? Whom does she approach today for shelter?

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvantaṃ rājānaṃ niśāyāṃ jīvalo 'bravīt kām enāṃ śocase nityaṃ śrotum icchāmi bāhuka
english: Hearing the king speak thus in the night, Jīvala said: For whom do you grieve constantly? I wish to hear, Bāhuka.

sanskrit: tam uvāca nalo rājā mandaprajñasya kasya cit āsīd bahumatā nārī tasyā dṛḍhataraṃ ca saḥ
english: King Nala replied to him: There was a woman dearly beloved of some fool of poor understanding; he was deeply devoted to her.

sanskrit: sa vai kena cid arthena tayā mando vyayujyata viprayuktaś ca mandātmā bhramaty asukhapīḍitaḥ
english: That fool was separated from her on some account; parted from her, that feeble-spirited one wanders, tormented by unhappiness.

sanskrit: dahyamānaḥ sa śokena divārātram atandritaḥ niśākāle smaraṃs tasyāḥ ślokam ekaṃ sma gāyati
english: Burning with grief day and night without rest, he sings this one verse in the night watches, remembering her.

sanskrit: sa vai bhraman mahīṃ sarvāṃ kva cid āsādya kiṃ cana vasaty anarhas tadduḥkhaṃ bhūya evānusaṃsmaran
english: Wandering over the whole earth, he has settled somewhere upon obtaining something — undeservedly, remembering again and again that same sorrow.

sanskrit: sā tu taṃ puruṣaṃ nārī kṛcchre 'py anugatā vane tyaktā tenālpapuṇyena duṣkaraṃ yadi jīvati
english: That woman who had followed that man even into the hardship of the forest — abandoned by that man of little merit — if she still lives, it is a hard thing.

sanskrit: ekā bālānabhijñā ca mārgāṇām atathocitā kṣutpipāsāparītā ca duṣkaraṃ yadi jīvati
english: Alone, inexperienced, unfit for such ways, overcome with hunger and thirst — if she still lives, it is a hard thing.

sanskrit: śvāpadācarite nityaṃ vane mahati dāruṇe tyaktā tenālpapuṇyena mandaprajñena māriṣa
english: In the great and dreadful forest frequented always by beasts of prey, abandoned by that feeble-minded man of little merit — O dear one.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ naiṣadho rājā damayantīm anusmaran ajñātavāsam avasad rājñas tasya niveśane
english: Thus it was that king Naiṣadha, ceaselessly remembering Damayantī, lived incognito in the residence of that king.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca hṛtarājye nale bhīmaḥ sabhārye preṣyatāṃ gate dvijān prasthāpayām āsa naladarśanakāṅkṣayā
english: Bṛhadaśva said: After Nala, with his kingdom lost, had gone into servitude along with his wife, Bhīma sent forth brahmin men, longing for news of Nala.

sanskrit: saṃdideśa ca tān bhīmo vasu dattvā ca puṣkalam mṛgayadhvaṃ nalaṃ caiva damayantīṃ ca me sutām
english: Bhīma instructed them and gave them abundant wealth, saying: Seek out both Nala and my daughter Damayantī.

sanskrit: asmin karmaṇi niṣpanne vijñāte niṣadhādhipe gavāṃ sahasraṃ dāsyāmi yo vas tāv ānayiṣyati agrahāraṃ ca dāsyāmi grāmaṃ nagarasaṃmitam
english: When this task is accomplished and the lord of Niṣadha is found — to him among you who brings them both, I will give a thousand cattle, and I will also grant a village the size of a city.

sanskrit: na cec chakyāv ihānetuṃ damayantī nalo 'pi vā jñātamātre 'pi dāsyāmi gavāṃ daśaśataṃ dhanam
english: And if Damayantī or Nala cannot be brought here, even for merely finding where they are I will give ten hundred cattle as wealth.

sanskrit: ity uktās te yayur hṛṣṭā brāhmaṇāḥ sarvatodiśam purarāṣṭrāṇi cinvanto naiṣadhaṃ saha bhāryayā
english: Thus instructed, those brahmin men went out joyfully in all directions, searching cities and kingdoms for Naiṣadha together with his wife.

sanskrit: tataś cedipurīṃ ramyāṃ sudevo nāma vai dvijaḥ vicinvāno 'tha vaidarbhīm apaśyad rājaveśmani puṇyāhavācane rājñaḥ sunandāsahitāṃ sthitām
english: Then a brahmin named Sudeva, searching the lovely city of Cedi, saw the daughter of Vidarbha standing in the royal palace at the auspicious recitation of the king, together with Sunandā.

sanskrit: mandaprakhyāyamānena rūpeṇāpratimena tām pinaddhāṃ dhūmajālena prabhām iva vibhāvasoḥ
english: Though her peerless beauty shone but dimly, she was like the radiance of the sun shrouded in a net of smoke.

sanskrit: tāṃ samīkṣya viśālākṣīm adhikaṃ malināṃ kṛśām tarkayām āsa bhaimīti kāraṇair upapādayan
english: Closely observing her — wide-eyed, exceedingly soiled, emaciated — he concluded by reasoned inference that this was the daughter of Bhīma.

sanskrit: sudeva uvāca yatheyaṃ me purā dṛṣṭā tathārūpeyam aṅganā kṛtārtho 'smy adya dṛṣṭvemāṃ lokakāntām iva śriyam
english: Sudeva said: This woman is exactly as I saw her before; I have achieved my purpose today in beholding this one who is like Śrī, beloved of all the world.

sanskrit: pūrṇacandrānanāṃ śyāmāṃ cāruvṛttapayodharām kurvantīṃ prabhayā devīṃ sarvā vitimirā diśaḥ
english: Her face is like the full moon, she is dark of complexion, her breasts beautifully rounded; by her radiance, O goddess, she renders all directions free of darkness.

sanskrit: cārupadmapalāśākṣīṃ manmathasya ratīm iva iṣṭāṃ sarvasya jagataḥ pūrṇacandraprabhām iva
english: Her eyes are lovely as lotus petals; she is like Rati, the beloved of Manmatha; beloved of all the world, she shines like the radiance of the full moon.

sanskrit: vidarbhasarasas tasmād daivadoṣād ivoddhṛtām malapaṅkānuliptāṅgīṃ mṛṇālīm iva tāṃ bhṛśam
english: She seems like a lotus stalk snatched from that lake of Vidarbha by the fault of fate, her limbs smeared heavily with the mud of filth.

sanskrit: paurṇamāsīm iva niśāṃ rāhugrastaniśākarām patiśokākulāṃ dīnāṃ śuṣkasrotāṃ nadīm iva
english: She is like a full-moon night when the moon is swallowed by Rāhu; overwhelmed with grief for her husband, wretched, she is like a river with dried-up streams.

sanskrit: vidhvastaparṇakamalāṃ vitrāsitavihaṃgamām hastihastaparikliṣṭāṃ vyākulām iva padminīm
english: She is like a lotus pond whose leaf-lotuses are ruined, whose birds have been frightened away, and which has been crushed by an elephant's trunk — agitated and distressed.

sanskrit: sukumārīṃ sujātāṅgīṃ ratnagarbhagṛhocitām dahyamānām ivoṣṇena mṛṇālīm aciroddhṛtām
english: She is tender, her limbs finely formed, fit to dwell in a jewel-laden palace — yet she is like a lotus stalk just torn from the water, scorched as if by heat.

sanskrit: rūpaudāryaguṇopetāṃ maṇḍanārhām amaṇḍitām candralekhām iva navāṃ vyomni nīlābhrasaṃvṛtām
english: Endowed with beauty, nobility, and virtue, worthy of adornment yet unadorned, she is like a fresh crescent moon in the sky covered by dark clouds.

sanskrit: kāmabhogaiḥ priyair hīnāṃ hīnāṃ bandhujanena ca dehaṃ dhārayatīṃ dīnāṃ bhartṛdarśanakāṅkṣayā
english: Deprived of the beloved pleasures of love, deprived of her kinsmen, wretched — she sustains her body in longing for the sight of her husband.
